en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Amitābha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of Kucha during the Yao Qin dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
At Jeta’s Grove, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, all of whom were great arhats well-known to the multitude.

The Elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Cūḍapanthaka, Nanda, Ānanda, Rāhula, Gavāmpati, Piṇḍola-bharadvāja, Kālodāyin, Mahākapphiṇa, Bakula, and Aniruddha—these and other great disciples, together with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Mañjuśrī the Dharma Prince, Ajita Bodhisattva, Gandhahasti Bodhisattva, and Nityodyukta Bodhisattva—and these and other great bodhisattvas, were present along with the vast assembly of devas, including Śakra Devendra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Elder Śāriputra:
"From here, passing through a hundred trillion buddha-fields to the west, there is a world named Sukhāvatī."
In that land there is a Buddha named Amitābha, who is currently dwelling there and preaching the Dharma.
Śāriputra, for what reason is that land called "Supreme Bliss" (Sukhāvatī)?
The sentient beings in that land have no manifold sufferings and experience only various joys; therefore, it is named "Ultimate Bliss" (Sukhāvatī).

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the land of Ultimate Bliss is surrounded on all sides by sevenfold railings, sevenfold nets, and sevenfold rows of trees, all made of the four precious substances; for this reason, that land is called Ultimate Bliss.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the land of Ultimate Bliss there are ponds made of the seven treasures, filled with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities; the bottoms of these ponds are entirely covered with ground of golden sand."
The stairways on its four sides are composed of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal;
above them are multi-storied pavilions, likewise adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musaragalva, red pearls, and agate.

In the pond, there are lotus flowers as large as chariot wheels; the blue ones emit blue light, the yellow ones yellow light, the red ones red light, and the white ones white light—subtle, wondrous, fragrant, and pure.
Śāriputra! The land of Sukhāvatī is thus adorned with such meritorious qualities.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In that Buddha-land, celestial music constantly plays, and the ground is made of gold; six times throughout the day and night, the heavens rain down *māndārava* flowers.
The sentient beings of that land regularly at dawn each take various wonderful flowers in their robes and bowls to make offerings to hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas in other directions;
then, at the time of the meal, they return to their own land to eat and practice walking meditation.
Śāriputra, the land of Ultimate Bliss is adorned with such meritorious qualities. Furthermore, Śāriputra:
In that land there are always various wonderful birds of diverse colors—white swans, peacocks, parrots, śāris, kalaviṅkas, and jīvañjīvakas.

These various birds, throughout the six periods of day and night, produce harmonious and elegant sounds; those sounds expound and clarify such dharmas as the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
When the sentient beings in that land hear these sounds, they all bring to mind the Buddha, the Dharma,
and the Sangha. Śāriputra,
do not think that these birds are actually born as a result of their karmic retribution for sins.
Why is this? Because, Śāriputra, in that Buddha-land there are no three evil realms of existence.
In that Buddha-land, even the names of the three evil realms do not exist, let alone their actual presence.
All these birds are transformations produced by Amitābha Buddha, intended to cause the sounds of the Dharma to circulate and flow forth.

Śāriputra! When the gentle breeze blows through that Buddha-land, the various rows of jewel trees and the jeweled nets produce sublime sounds, like a hundred thousand kinds of music playing simultaneously. Those who hear these sounds will all spontaneously give rise to thoughts of mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Saṅgha.
"Śāriputra! That buddha-field is adorned with such accomplished merits and virtues. Śāriputra!"
"What do you think?
For what reason is that Buddha named Amitābha?
"Śāriputra! [the Buddha said.]
The light of that Buddha is immeasurable; it illuminates the lands of the ten directions without obstruction, and for this reason he is named Amitābha.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the lifespan of that Buddha and of his people shall last for immeasurable, boundless, asaṃkhyeya kalpas; therefore, he is named Amitāyus.
Śāriputra! Since Amitābha Buddha attained Buddhahood, ten kalpas have passed until now.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
That Buddha has immeasurable and boundless śrāvaka disciples, all of whom are arhats, beyond what can be known by calculation;
the bodhisattvas are likewise so.
Śāriputra! That Buddha-land is adorned with such accomplished merits and virtues.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Those beings who are born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss are all *avaivartika* (non-retrogressive).

Among them, there are many who are in their last birth before Buddhahood (*ekajātipratibaddha*), so numerous that they cannot be known by calculation; they can only be described as being immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) for countless *kalpas*.
Śāriputra! Those sentient beings who hear this should make a vow, vowing to be born in that land. Why is this?
"To be able to assemble in one place together with such superior and virtuous people—
Śāriputra, one cannot attain birth in that land through small roots of goodness or causes and conditions of merit."

Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who, upon hearing the teaching of Amitābha Buddha, hold fast to his name for one day, two days, three days, four days, five days, six days, or seven days, with single-mindedness and without distraction.
When that person approaches the end of their life, Amitābha Buddha, together with a multitude of holy beings, will appear before them.
At the moment of death, this person’s mind will not be inverted, and they will immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha.
Śāriputra! It is because I see this benefit that I have spoken these words.
If there are sentient beings who hear this teaching, they should make a vow to be born in that land.
“Śāriputra! Just as I now praise the inconceivable merit of Amitābha Buddha, so too in the eastern direction there are Buddhas such as Akṣobhya Buddha,

Sumerukūṭa Buddha, Mahāsumeru Buddha, Sumeruprabhāsa Buddha, and Gadgadasvara Buddha— Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River— who each, in their respective lands, extend their broad and long tongues to completely cover the trichiliocosm, speaking words of truth:”
“You sentient beings, you should believe in this Sutra on the Praise of the Inconceivable Merit and the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas. “Śāriputra!

In the worlds of the southern direction, there are Buddhas such as Candrasūryapradīpa, Yaśaḥprabha, Mahārciskandha, Merupradīpa, and Anantavīrya—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—who each, in their respective lands, extend their broad and long tongues until they completely cover the trichiliocosm, and speak these words of truth:
"You sentient beings, you should believe this Sutra on the Inconceivable Merit of Recitation, which is protected and remembered by all Buddhas."

“Śāriputra! In the western world-system there are Buddhas such as Amitāyus, Amitābha, Amitadhvaja, Mahāprabha, Mahārciskandha, Ratnaketu, and Śuddharaśmiprabha—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each, in his own land, extends his broad and long tongue until it completely covers the trichiliocosm, and speaks these truthful words:
‘You sentient beings, you must believe this Sūtra on the Praise of Inconceivable Merit, which is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas.’”

“Śāriputra! In the worlds of the northern direction, there are Buddhas such as Flame-Shoulder Buddha, Most Victorious Sound Buddha, Unassailable Buddha, Sun-Born Buddha, and Net-Illumination Buddha—Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. Each, in his own land, extends his broad and long tongue, covering the entire trichiliocosm, and speaks these words of truth:
‘You sentient beings, you must believe this Sūtra which praises inconceivable merit and is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas.’”

“Śāriputra! In the worlds below there are Buddhas—Siṃha Buddha, Yaśas Buddha, Yaśaskīrti Buddha, Dharmakīrti Buddha, Dharmadhvaja Buddha, and Dharmadhara Buddha—and other Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each, in his own land, extends his broad and long tongue until it completely covers the trichiliocosm, and speaks these truthful words:
‘You sentient beings, you should believe this Sūtra on the Inconceivable Merit of Praise, which is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas.’”

“Śāriputra! In the worlds above, there are Buddhas such as Brahmā-voice Buddha, Constellation King Buddha, Fragrance Supreme Buddha, Fragrant Light Buddha, Great Flame Shoulder Buddha, Adorned-body-with-various-colored-jewel-flowers Buddha, Śāla-tree-king Buddha, Jewel-flower-virtue Buddha, Seeing-all-meanings Buddha, and Tathāgata-like-Sumeru-mountain Buddha. These and other Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each from their respective lands, extend their broad and long tongues until they completely cover the trichiliocosm, and speak these words of truth:
‘You sentient beings, you should believe this Sūtra on the Inconceivable Merit Praised by All Buddhas and Protected by the Mindfulness of All Buddhas.’”
“Śāriputra! What do you think? For what reason is it called ‘The Sūtra Protected and Mindfully Kept by All Buddhas’?”
Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who, upon hearing this sutra, accept and uphold it, or who hear the names of the various Buddhas—
these good men and good women shall all be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas together, and they shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Therefore, Śāriputra!
You all should believe and accept my words as well as what has been spoken by all the Buddhas. Śāriputra!
If there are those who have already made the vow, are now making the vow, or will make the vow, desiring to be born in the land of Amitābha Buddha—
all such persons shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, whether they have already been born, are now being born, or will be born in that land.
Therefore, Śāriputra, if there are sons or daughters of good family who possess faith, they should make a vow to be born in that land. Śāriputra!

Just as I now praise the inconceivable merit of all Buddhas, so too do those Buddhas proclaim my own inconceivable merit, saying: "Śākyamuni Buddha has been able to perform a most difficult and rare feat;

in this Sahā world-system, amidst the five turbidities—the turbidity of the kalpa, the turbidity of views, the turbidity of afflictions, the turbidity of sentient beings, and the turbidity of life—he has attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and preaches for the sake of all sentient beings this Dharma that is difficult for all the worlds to believe."

"Śāriputra! You should know that in this world of five turbidities, I have performed this difficult task: having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I preach this dharma so difficult to believe for the sake of all the worlds; this is truly most difficult!"

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Śāriputra, the bhikṣus, and all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and others—hearing what the Buddha had taught, rejoiced with faith and acceptance, prostrated themselves, and departed.
The Buddha-spoken *Amitābha Sūtra*: The Dhāraṇī for Rebirth in the Pure Land Spoken by Amitāyus Buddha:

*Namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya | tadyathā | amṛtodbhave amṛte svadhāvini amṛte vikaraṇe gamini gagane jitakāli svāhā* Whoever recites this dhāraṇī, Amitābha Buddha will constantly abide upon their crown; after the end of life, they will spontaneously attain rebirth [in the Pure Land].
Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna aspired to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī) and was moved by this dhāraṇī in a dream.
The Tripiṭaka Master Yaśas recited this dhāraṇī, and Dharma Master Xiū of Tiānpíng Monastery received it orally from the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśas.
The person said:
"The original sūtra has not come from foreign lands.
As for the method of upholding the dhāraṇī, one should recite it twenty-one times during each of the six periods of the day and night."
Morning and night, one should wash and rinse the mouth, chew *śītalā* twigs, burn incense and lamps, kneel before an image, and with palms joined, recite [the name] twenty-one times.
If one does this constantly every day, the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and the sin of slandering the Vaipulya sutras will all be extinguished.
In this present life, one will not be troubled or disturbed by any malevolent ghosts or spirits, and after the end of life, one will naturally be reborn in the Land of Amitābha.
How much more inconceivable are the merits of upholding and reciting [this] day and night!
The Shorter Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra, Scroll One.
